validated_incidents.title: Richland helicopter-like object with stationary rotor
validated_incidents.summary: An observer in Richland, Washington used a telescope to observe a shimmering speck at extreme altitude that appeared helicopter-like with a stationary rotor. One object darted away to the west and disappeared; another was observed continuously for two minutes until it disappeared.
validated_incidents.raw_excerpt: At about 14:30 hours we sighted a bright shimmering speck at very extreme altitude, perhaps 30,000 feet perhaps much lower. This speck hovered at a north azimuth to Richland of about 80 degrees, I tried to pick up the object in the telescope and while trying to locate it in the very small field, about 15 minutes angle, my friend located another similar speck a Short distance away. At this time we were convinced that they were birds, but had not yet sighted one in the glass because of the small field. Suddenly one of the specks ceased hovering and darted off to the west and disappeared.
validated_incidents.shape_description: bright shimmering speck, resembled helicopter with rotor stationary

validated_incidents.title: Half-moon shaped objects over Pasco, Washington
validated_incidents.summary: Two half-moon shaped objects, estimated six times larger than a half moon, were observed near Pasco, Washington. One object formed into a large fireball while the other split into two fireballs, both at approximately 1000 feet altitude and observed for ten minutes.
validated_incidents.raw_excerpt: GAIL PECK, Pasco, Wash., Phone Pasco 6054, supervisor of a local ground observer group at pasco, reported sighting two half-moon shaped objects about six times as large as a half moon. One object formed into a large fhre-ball, the original color of both objects was white, and the other formed into two fireballs. Both objects were estimated to be at about 1000 feet altitude.
validated_incidents.size_description: about six times as large as a half moon

validated_incidents.title: TIMOTHY Radar and F-86D Airborne Interception, June 1954
validated_incidents.summary: Multiple radar blips were detected on TIMOTHY radar scope over a ten-minute period on 22 June 1954. Two F-86D fighter interceptors (Pronto Blue #1 and #2) were vectored to intercept; Blue #2 tracked a target descending from 25,000 to 6,000 feet at speeds up to 0.9 Mach before the blip separated into two distinct returns and disappeared from scope.
validated_incidents.raw_excerpt: An unknown blip or target was picked up on TIMOTHY radar control scope in Georef LE 1604, estimated 200 knot speed, estimated altitude 15 angles, originally at 0314Z and intermittently thereafter for a total of three (3) sightings by TIMOTHY within a ten (10) minute period after which time blip or target remained off. Pronto Blue #2 obtained an airborne reader pickup lower left portion scope, approximately twenty-eight (28) miles from blip or target which separated into two "clear distinct" blips at 04352; altitude 25,000 feet. Blue #2 attempted to close on 30 degree port heading in attempt to center blip, descending from 25,000 feet to 6,000 feet and to within estimated six (6) miles with speed increasing from .85 to .9 Mach.
validated_incidents.location_text: Georef LE 1604, vicinity of TIMOTHY radar control site
validated_incidents.reporting_unit: 20th District Office of Special Investigations, McChord Air Force Base; 25th Air Division; 317th Fighter Interceptor Squadron
validated_incidents.resolution_notes: Malfunction of radar was ruled out by site Tech Representative. Weather balloons, boats, ships, and aircraft were excluded through checks with weather stations, Seattle AMIS, Navy, Coast Guard, and 5 ADDC. One Navy P2V found flying over 100 miles away.

validated_incidents.title: Spherical Metal Ball Observed Over Kennewick, Washington
validated_incidents.summary: Sergeant Gordon Richardson of the Kennewick Police Department reported observing a large, shining metal ball approximately 30 feet in diameter traveling at high speed over Kennewick, Washington about a year before June 1956. The object came to a complete stop, emitted a trail of fire, then accelerated rapidly and disappeared.

The ball was travelling at a high rate of spped and when it got abauit three blocks east of Jashington Street it came to a complete stop. RICHARDSON ststed ths the ball had left 4 tail of fire until it stopped and then emitted no fire or smoke.
validated_incidents.location_text: vicinity of 1st and Washington, Kennewick, Washington
validated_incidents.reporting_unit: District Commander, 20th District, OSI, McChord Air Force Base
validated_incidents.shape_description: perfectly spherical, large shining metal ball
validated_incidents.resolution_notes: Witness theorized the craft used principles of electromagnetism or electron beams to defy gravity; noted object was flying too low for radar detection and too fast for interception by known US aircraft.
